extracted.intended_audience: general public, law students, and legal information seekers (those researching tort/product liability cases)
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedia-style summary of the 1994 Liebeck v. McDonald’s product liability case, covering liability findings, damages, factual background (temperature, injuries, prior complaints), and the ensuing public debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product liability — dangerously hot product
rubrics_metrics.description: A jury found McDonald’s liable for selling a dangerously hot product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes the finding of liability was based on the coffee being served at an unsafe temperature and causing severe injury; this criterion is supported by factual evidence such as the serving temperature (nearly 190 degrees) and prior similar complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensatory damages — medical and compensatory award
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury awarded $200,000 in compensatory damages (reduced to $160,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensatory damages cover actual losses (medical costs, pain and suffering). The example shows compensatory awards can be adjusted downward to account for plaintiff fault (see comparative fault entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative fault — reduction for plaintiff's fault
rubrics_metrics.description: The compensatory award was reduced to $160,000 due to Liebeck's 20% fault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This illustrates that a plaintiff's own negligence or fault can proportionally reduce compensatory damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punitive damages — punishment and remittitur
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury awarded $2.7 million in punitive damages; the trial court later suggested reducing the punitive award to $480,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punitive damages are intended to punish particularly reprehensible conduct and to deter future wrongdoing; courts may remit (reduce) excessive punitive awards before final judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severity of injury — extent and treatment of harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Liebeck suffered severe burns requiring skin grafting and hospitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The seriousness of physical injury is a key factor in assessing compensatory and punitive damages, and in establishing the real-world harm caused by the product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior similar complaints / defendant knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: McDonald's had prior similar complaints about the temperature of its coffee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence that a defendant had prior complaints or notice about a hazard supports claims of negligence and can justify punitive damages for continuing a dangerous practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serving temperature relative to industry — unreasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: McDonald's served coffee at nearly 190 degrees, hotter than competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviation from industry norms or customary practices (e.g., serving temperature) can be used to show the product was unreasonably dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaintiff's initial settlement offer — mitigation and reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: Liebeck initially offered to settle for less than her medical costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A plaintiff's attempt to settle for medical costs may bear on perceptions of reasonableness and may be relevant evidence in assessing the parties' conduct pre-litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public debate and media portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: The case sparked public debate about tort reform and has often been misunderstood or misrepresented in the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a legal standard, the page highlights how media portrayal and public opinion can shape perceptions of a case and influence broader policy debates about litigation and damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process: jury finding and trial court action (remittitur) / settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: A jury found liability and set damages; the trial court suggested reducing the punitive award; the case later settled confidentially before final judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This illustrates the roles of jury verdicts, judicial review/remittitur of awards, and settlement—process-level considerations that affect final outcomes in tort litigation.
